subject: physical-education
successCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about judging effort without measurement at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for judging effort without measurement.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
scoringGuidance: Score cue use, control, decision-making, and explanation. Never score speed, distance, repetitions, body measurement, or comparison with another learner. Choosing the adapted path, a rest, or an opt-out is never scored as a deficit. Never infer effort, character, or ability from a movement outcome.
masteryRule: Do not mark mastery from one attempt. Use observed control, cue use, decision-making, explanation, and applied performance; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer on at least two separate occasions. Mastery is never determined by speed, distance, repetition count, body measurement, or comparison with another learner.
remediation: Return to the simplest version of judging effort without measurement — slower, closer, larger, or supported — then retry one fresh attempt.

adaptiveRoutes.action: Return to the simplest version of judging effort without measurement — slower, closer, larger, or supported — then retry one fresh attempt.
Ask the learner to name the cue for judging effort without measurement and say why it works before continuing.
Confirm the specific cue the learner executed well for judging effort without measurement, offer one varied condition, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, never as a comment on the learner body, effort, or character, contrast it with a demonstration, and schedule short varied practice.
Require controlled independent performance of judging effort without measurement plus an explanation on a later or different occasion before marking it mastered.

guardianOrParentVisibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, the guardian safety confirmation for equipment and environment, and the next instructional step. Do not expose recordings, images, body data, or health information. Study records completion and progress metadata only; it does not perform or persist physical measurement or fitness tracking.

guardianSafetyReview.equipment: Body-weight activity only; water available throughout. No weights, no measurement device, no fitness-test equipment.
guardianSafetyReview.environment: Indoor open space or a supervised outdoor area with shade and water access.
guardianSafetyReview.movement_hazards: Sustained activity raises heart rate and body temperature. Guardian confirms hydration, allows rest at any time, and adjusts for heat, asthma, or any medical guidance already in place.
guardianSafetyReview.food_or_allergy_note: Guardian applies any existing medical guidance for exercise-related asthma, allergy, or condition. The course never asks for the diagnosis itself.

safetyAndPrivacyNotes: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, size, speed, and coordination.
Never require or record body weight, height, BMI, body-fat percentage, or any body measurement.
Never require a fitness test, a timed trial, a repetition count, a distance score, or any ranking of one learner against another.
Never require a photograph, video, or any recording of the learner as proof of participation or performance.
Never require a public performance, an audience, or a demonstration in front of peers; sharing is always the learner choice.
Progress is compared only against the learner own earlier work, and only when the learner chooses to track it.
Allow rest, a break, an adapted path, or an opt-out at any point without treating it as failure.
Stop activity and seek a trusted adult or qualified professional for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, or injury; this course is not medical advice.
